subject.title: Show DeepSeek Platform usage with cost summary

question: Should enabling Cost summary for DeepSeek be treated as consent to run the existing selected-Chrome-profile detailed Platform usage probe for users who previously left credits/extras disabled?
rationale: The patch intentionally reassigns an existing browser-session-backed probe to a different persisted preference; source-level tests establish the mechanics but cannot establish the intended privacy and upgrade contract.

options.title: Approve Cost summary as consent
options.body: Treat Cost summary as the canonical DeepSeek detailed-usage control, retain the active-account restriction, and document or make the setting meaning clear before merge.

options.title: Preserve the prior extra-usage opt-in
options.body: Require both Cost summary and the existing credits/extras preference so upgrading users do not begin the Platform probe under a newly broadened setting.

options.title: Add a DeepSeek-specific control
options.body: Keep Cost summary for display style but introduce an explicit DeepSeek detailed-Platform-data consent setting if the two concepts should remain independent.

recommendation.title: Approve Cost summary as consent
recommendation.body: Treat Cost summary as the canonical DeepSeek detailed-usage control, retain the active-account restriction, and document or make the setting meaning clear before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Zihao-Qi authored the merged DeepSeek detailed-usage implementation and this follow-up, making them the strongest available routing contact for the setting semantics.
